dashboard.title: Dashboard Help
dashboard.content:
The Dashboard shows the sync status of all your profiles at a glance.

**Status Card** — The overall state (idle, pushing, pulling, syncing or error), the most recent sync and the number of unsynced changes.

**System Health** — Shows if rclone is installed, your remote is reachable, and the database is healthy.

**Push / Pull buttons** — Act on every enabled profile, after a confirmation that shows how many files each sync would delete. Push makes the cloud folder an exact copy of your local folder (files that exist only in the cloud are deleted). Pull makes your local folder an exact copy of the cloud folder (files that exist only locally are deleted). Replaced and deleted files are kept in .omnisync-trash in the destination, and a sync that would delete more files than the profile's delete limit (shown in the confirmation) stops.

**Profiles** — Each row shows a profile's state; if its last sync failed or was refused, the reason is shown under it.

**Getting started:**
1. Add a remote on the Remotes page (e.g. your Google Drive)
2. Create a profile with a local and a remote directory
3. Come back here and Push or Pull

config.title: Configuration Help
config.content:
This page lets you configure OmniSync settings and cloud remotes.

**Local directory** — The folder on your computer to sync (e.g. /home/alice/Documents). Use the full path as it appears on your machine — OmniSync handles the Docker mapping automatically.

**Remote directory** — Where files go in the cloud. Format: `remotename:path` (e.g. `gdrive:backup/docs`). The part after the colon is a folder path on the remote — it will be created if it doesn't exist.

**Debounce** — How many seconds to wait after a file change before syncing. Prevents syncing on every keystroke.

**Pull interval** — How often (in minutes) to automatically check the cloud for new files.

**Remotes** — Cloud storage connections. Use the Setup Wizard on the Remotes page to add one.

jobs.title: Job History Help
jobs.content:
Every time OmniSync runs a sync (push or pull), it creates a job record.

**Direction** — Whether files were pushed (uploaded), pulled (downloaded), synced both ways (Two-way) or resynced (Resync: the union of both folders).

**Status** — Running, completed, or failed.

**Files changed** — How many files were created, updated, or deleted.

**Conflicts** — Files that were modified both locally and in the cloud at the same time.

**Click a job** to see the full list of files that were affected.

logs.title: Logs Help
logs.content:
The log viewer shows what OmniSync has been doing behind the scenes.

**Filter by level** — Use the tabs to show only specific log levels:
• DEBUG — Detailed technical info
• INFO — Normal operations (sync started, completed)
• WARNING — Something unexpected but not critical
• ERROR — Something went wrong

**Filter by category** — All entries, User actions (the audit trail: syncs started, profiles changed, remotes deleted, backups restored, with the client address), or Errors only.

An error message in the UI may end in an ID; the entry with the same Request ID here belongs to it.

Logs are useful for troubleshooting when syncs fail or files aren't appearing where expected.

conflicts.title: Conflicts Help
conflicts.content:
Conflicts happen when the same file is changed both locally and in the cloud between two syncs. Running a diff (the profile's Differences tab) lists every such file here.

**Keep local** — Copies the local file over the cloud copy. The cloud version is moved to .omnisync-trash on the remote.

**Keep remote** — Copies the cloud file over the local copy. The local version is moved to .omnisync-trash in the local folder.

**Keep both** — Both versions are kept on both sides, the cloud version under a new name (.conflict-<date>).

**Dismiss** — Only removes the entry from this list; no file is changed.

Each action asks for confirmation first, and the profile must be enabled. If a file changed again since the diff, nothing is overwritten: run the diff again. If you're unsure, "Keep both" is the safest option.

**Two-way conflicts** — When a two-way sync finds a file changed on both sides, it has already kept both versions on both sides (e.g. report.local-conflict1.txt next to report.txt). Keep only local / Keep only remote keeps one version under the original name and moves the other to .omnisync-trash; Keep both closes the entry and leaves both files.

profiles.title: Profiles Help
profiles.content:
Sync Profiles let you manage multiple independent sync configurations.

**Each profile** has its own local directory, remote directory, and sync settings. Profiles sync independently — you can push/pull each one separately.

**Create a profile** by clicking the Create Profile button and filling in the local and remote directories.

**Enable/disable** profiles using the toggle switch on each card. Disabled profiles won't sync automatically but keep their configuration.

**Per-profile settings** like debounce, pull interval, and rclone filters are configured when editing a profile.

**Sync mode** — Two-way (recommended, the default for new profiles) carries the changes on either side to the other and keeps both versions of a file changed on both sides. Mirror only pushes local changes and pulls the remote on the interval; the side that syncs last wins. Push and Pull stay available in both modes as confirmed one-way overrides.

**Resync** — The first two-way sync, and a sync after the two-way state was lost, is a resync: both folders become the union of both and nothing is deleted. A profile that needs one shows "Resync needed" and waits for your confirmation.

remotes.title: Remotes Help
remotes.content:
Remotes are the cloud storage connections rclone uses (Google Drive, S3, SFTP, …).

**Setup Wizard** — Creates a new remote. Pick a provider, enter its settings or sign in, and the wizard tests the connection. Besides the cloud providers it offers WebDAV (Nextcloud, ownCloud, SharePoint, …), SMB (Windows shares) and crypt, which encrypts file contents and names before they reach another remote.

**Test** — Checks that the remote is reachable and shows the latency.

**Storage** — Used and free space, when the provider reports it.

**Used by** — The profiles and backup targets that use this remote. Deleting a remote that is in use breaks them, so you are asked to confirm.

**Edit** — Changes the settings of a remote with keys or a password, or of a crypt remote, in place; the profiles that use it keep working. Stored secrets are never shown: leave a secret field empty to keep it, or tick its checkbox to remove it.

**Reconnect** — Renews the sign-in of a Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive remote that expired or was revoked. Only the token is replaced. When the last test, health check or sync was refused by the provider, the card gets a red border and an alert.

**Import rclone.conf** — Upload or paste an existing rclone.conf to see the remotes it holds. Names that are already taken can be imported under another name. Local remotes, remotes that wrap a local path, and remotes with `ssh` or `bearer_token_command` options are refused. Then import the ones you choose.

syncMode.label: Sync mode

two_way.label: Two-way (recommended)
two_way.desc: Changes on either side are carried to the other. Edits made offline and new files on both sides are kept, deletions are carried both ways (the deleted file is kept in that side's .omnisync-trash), and a file changed on both sides keeps both versions.

mirror.label: Mirror: one-way push/pull only
mirror.desc: Local changes are pushed to the remote, and the remote is pulled on the interval. The side that syncs last wins: a file that exists on only one side can be deleted by the next mirror.

syncMode.switchToTwoWayNote: After saving, the next sync is a resync: both folders become the union of both, and nothing is deleted.
syncMode.switchToMirrorNote: After saving, the two-way sync state is forgotten. From then on the side that syncs last wins.

twoWay.resyncExplain: A resync starts two-way syncing afresh from what is in both folders now.
twoWay.resyncUnion: Both folders become the union of both: a file that exists on only one side is copied to the other. Nothing is deleted.
twoWay.resyncNewer: Where a file differs, the newer version wins and the older one is moved to .omnisync-trash.
twoWay.resyncRequiredExplain: Automatic syncing of this profile is paused: its two-way sync state was lost or is inconsistent, for example after an interrupted sync. Confirm a resync to continue; it deletes nothing.
twoWay.switchHint: This profile mirrors one way, so the side that syncs last wins. Two-way keeps the changes from both sides.
twoWay.switchFirstRun: The first two-way sync is a resync: both folders become the union of both, and nothing is deleted. Where a file differs, the newer version wins and the older one is moved to .omnisync-trash.

mirrorNotice.title: This profile syncs as a mirror
mirrorNotice.what: Mirror mode copies one way at a time: a push makes the remote match this folder, and a pull makes this folder match the remote.
mirrorNotice.risk: Whichever runs next overwrites or deletes changes that exist only on the other side, for example edits made while syncing was paused or offline. Replaced and deleted files are kept in .omnisync-trash.
mirrorNotice.twoWay: Two-way sync keeps the changes from both sides. Its first run is a resync: both folders become the union of both, and nothing is deleted.
mirrorNotice.dashboardTitle: Profiles that sync as a mirror
mirrorNotice.dashboardIntro: These profiles copy one way at a time: push and pull each make one side match the other, so changes made on the other side while syncing was paused or offline can be overwritten or deleted (they are kept in .omnisync-trash).
mirrorNotice.switchAll: Switch all mirror profiles to two-way
mirrorNotice.switchAllTitle: Switch all mirror profiles to two-way?
mirrorNotice.switchAllDone_one: {{count}} profile now syncs two-way. Its next sync is a resync that deletes nothing.
mirrorNotice.switchAllDone_other: {{count}} profiles now sync two-way. The next sync of each is a resync that deletes nothing.

auth.title: Log in to OmniSync
auth.description: This web UI is protected by a password.
auth.throttled_one: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{count}} second.
auth.throttled_other: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{count}} seconds.
auth.misconfigured: The login is not set up correctly. Check the web UI server log.
auth.failed: Could not reach the server. Please try again.

pause.pauseHelp: Pause automatic syncing of this profile until you resume it. Syncs you start still run.
pause.pauseAllHelp: Pause automatic syncing of every profile until you resume. Syncs you start still run.
pause.resumeAllHelp: Resume the profiles you paused. Profiles OmniSync paused to protect your files stay paused until you review them.
pause.bannerByUser: You paused automatic syncing. Changes are not synced until you resume; syncs you start still run.

syncLimits.bwlimitHelp: Optional. A rate such as 10M or 512k, or a timetable such as 08:00,512k 19:00,10M 23:00,off (rclone --bwlimit).
syncLimits.bwlimitInvalid: Not a valid limit. Use e.g. 10M, 512k, off, 10M:1M or 08:00,512k 19:00,10M 23:00,off.
syncLimits.bwlimitTwice: --bwlimit is also set in the rclone arguments. Remove one of them.
syncLimits.windowHelp: Automatic syncs run only at these times. Syncs you start run at any time.
syncLimits.windowInvalid: Enter a start and an end time that differ.
syncLimits.windowNote: Server time. An end before the start runs past midnight (e.g. 22:00 to 06:00). Changes made outside the window are synced when it opens.
syncLimits.closed: Outside the sync window: automatic syncs wait.
syncLimits.waiting: Outside the sync window: a sync is waiting for it to open.

folderPicker.title: Choose folders to sync
folderPicker.explain: Uncheck the folders to leave out. The choice is written as filter rules below, which you can still edit.
folderPicker.replacesRules: The current folder rules cannot be shown here and will be replaced. Other rules (e.g. - *.tmp) are kept.
folderPicker.markerKept: Two-way: OmniSync keeps its sync marker .omnisync-check included on its own.

trash.title: Trash
trash.explain: Files a sync replaced or deleted are kept here, in .omnisync-trash. Restore puts a file back where it was; the next sync carries it to the other side.
trash.confirmDelete: They are removed from the trash and cannot be restored.
trash.confirmOverwriteTitle_one: {{count}} file is newer at its original place
trash.confirmOverwriteTitle_other: {{count}} files are newer at their original place
trash.confirmOverwrite: Replace them with the trashed versions? The current versions are moved to the trash first, so nothing is lost.
